title: Image Upload and Storage Exercise
prompt:
Allow authenticated uploads, validate them, protect private files, and render appropriate image URLs.

Submission: a small reviewable artifact, relevant tests, expected outputs, one failure/boundary case, and version/environment notes. Use synthetic data. Django/Python server code is not executed by CodeLeaf browser preview; local or human review is required.
target_skills: Limit upload size and allowed content types using layered checks.
Store media separately from static files and keep private assets protected.
Test invalid, oversized, and authorized download cases.

starter.content:
from django import forms

class ImageUploadForm(forms.Form):
    image = forms.ImageField()
    # Add a validated size limit in clean_image() for your policy.

expected_output: ImageField requires Pillow; do not install unreviewed dependencies just to run this snippet.
acceptance_criteria: A valid image follows the configured storage path.
Private media cannot be retrieved by unauthorized users.
State whether verification was local, static, or human-reviewed.
Do not claim a build/deployment or external integration was tested unless it was actually run.
hints: Never trust the supplied filename/extension as proof of safe content.
Use request.FILES and an upload form.
Plan storage permissions, malware/content scanning, and cleanup.
grading_method: Required-string smoke check plus human review of technical correctness, tests, safe handling, expected result and reproducibility. This does not execute arbitrary Python/Django code.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed after reviewing feedback; the platform backend owns its uniform XP/idempotency rules.
